# v2.93

**This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases v2.91-dev, v2.92-dev and
v2.93-dev.** It is a security release throughout, and it closes out the review
that began with v2.88. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes below say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong.

Nothing here needs configuring. There are no database changes, and every new
setting is optional with a sensible default.

## Fixed

- **The daily credential health check now actually runs.** The scheduled job that
  keeps the Box / OneDrive / Google Drive / SMTP status badges and the expiry
  banner up to date was being turned away before it reached the application, so
  those statuses only ever refreshed when someone pressed **Test Connection** or
  a scheduled export happened to run. If you have cloud credentials connected,
  expect the health panel to become accurate within a day of updating.

- **A suspended account could still change its own sign-in security settings.**
  Disabling a user takes effect immediately everywhere else, but the two-factor
  setup and confirmation steps were not checking it, so a disabled account could
  still generate and confirm a new authenticator code — and where two-factor had
  been made mandatory for that user, finish the process and get a working
  session. Both steps now refuse for a disabled or ended session. Normal
  enrolment is unaffected.

## Hardened

### Restoring a backup

- **Restoring now asks you to confirm it's really you.** Both the upload restore
  and the "restore a saved backup" flow require you to re-enter your **own
  account password** — and a current MFA code if your account uses MFA — before
  the restore runs. Being signed in is no longer enough on its own. Keep your
  credentials to hand when restoring.

- **A backup that carries user accounts is only accepted when it's encrypted.**
  User credentials are only ever written into an encrypted backup, so an
  unencrypted file that nonetheless claims to include accounts is corrupt or was
  altered, and the restore refuses it rather than trusting the account data
  inside. Ordinary backups — encrypted standard backups, passphrase-protected
  portable backups, and credential-free backups — restore exactly as before.

- **Uploaded backups have a size limit** (512 MB by default, adjustable with the
  new optional `BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB` setting), checked before the file is read
  into memory.

### Scheduled jobs and imports

- **Scheduled jobs now prove themselves per request.** The internal
  authentication used by the automatic backup, export and credential-check jobs
  previously produced one value that was good for every one of those jobs for a
  whole day. It is now tied to the individual request and to a short time window,
  and is accepted only once, so it cannot be observed and reused. `CRON_SECRET`
  is unchanged.

- **Imports reject oversized and malformed uploads properly.** Every import
  endpoint checks the size of the data before reading it in (32 MB by default,
  adjustable with the new optional `IMPORT_MAX_BODY_MB` setting) and returns a
  clear message for a file that is too large or a request that isn't valid import
  data, instead of a generic server error.

- **Two-factor setup and backup restore are now rate-limited**, the same way
  sign-in and the other password prompts already were.

### Keeping it that way

- **Permission checks on every API route are now verified automatically.** A new
  check runs on every change and fails if any route is missing its permission
  check, naming the route. Routes deliberately reachable without signing in — the
  login page's logo, the sign-in call itself, and first-run setup — must be
  listed explicitly with a written reason, so "nobody noticed this route was
  public" stops being possible. There are six such routes and every one is
  accounted for. The check also confirms the server's scheduled jobs are wired up
  consistently at both ends, which is the specific mistake behind the credential
  health check above.

- **A company-scoped report query now fails safe** rather than ignoring the
  company filter if it were ever called with an empty selection. No page reached
  it that way, so no data was exposed; the guard stops a future caller
  reintroducing the possibility.

## Also verified this release

Checks run and recorded, with no changes needed:

- Every backup format was inspected for anything that should never leave the
  server. Stored delivery credentials (SMTP passwords, cloud tokens) and API keys
  appear in **none** of them. User sign-in details appear only when "Include user
  credentials" is ticked, and only ever inside an encrypted file — confirmed by
  also testing what happens when no encryption key is configured.
- Security headers were confirmed present on every kind of response, including
  the public API and the pre-sign-in branding images.

## Upgrading

The update applies automatically; there are no database changes.

- **Restoring a backup now prompts for your password** (and MFA code if you use
  one). Nothing to configure — just have them to hand.
- `BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB` and `IMPORT_MAX_BODY_MB` are optional, documented in
  `.env.example`, and the defaults suit typical installs.
- The scheduled-job change updates the app and its cron scripts together. If a
  job happens to fire during the few minutes between the files updating and the
  service restarting, that one run is skipped and logged — exports retry the next
  minute, and the credential check the next day.

All of the above is reflected in the README and the in-app help
(**Backup & Restore**, **Import Data**, **Scheduled Report Exports**).
